findings.highlight: Her neck is half cut off
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーのように首を半分以上削がれ
findings.governingReading: Like Rider, more than half her neck has been gouged away
findings.explanation: The comparison to Rider and the fact that the wound exceeds half the neck both disappear.

findings.highlight: Saber is in a terrible situation right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今のセイバーは死に体だ
findings.governingReading: Saber is as good as dead now
findings.explanation: Saber’s moribund condition is reduced to generic danger.

findings.evidenceJa: 葛木の脇をすり抜けながら木刀を一閃する
findings.governingReading: As I slip past Kuzuki’s side, I flash the wooden sword through one stroke
findings.explanation: The movement past Kuzuki, weapon identity, and single cutting action all disappear.

findings.highlight: deprives me of my left foot
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の足許を[ruby text=・・・・・ o2o=1]奪っていき
findings.explanation: A blow that destroys Shirou’s base and movement is mistranslated as removing his left foot.

findings.evidenceJa: 俺の足許を奪っていき
findings.governingReading: takes my footing out from under me
findings.explanation: The mature-text branch converts loss of footing into explicit amputation absent from the active Japanese prose.

findings.highlight: A hammer-like fist strikes her head
findings.evidenceJa: 城壁を穿つ[ruby text=つち]槌めいた一撃
findings.governingReading: A hammer-like blow capable of punching through a castle wall buries itself in her face
findings.explanation: The attack’s scale, written hammer/read mallet layer, and exact facial impact are weakened.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka’s head isn’t there. Anything above her neck doesn’t exist anymore.
findings.evidenceJa: そこに遠坂の顔が見えない
findings.governingReading: Tohsaka’s face is no longer visible there
findings.explanation: The mature-text branch replaces the source’s viewpoint-bound absence of her face with explicit total decapitation and adds a second unsupported sentence.

findings.highlight: a student who’s unable to answer his question in a classroom
findings.evidenceJa: 答えが解らず俯く生徒のように
findings.governingReading: like a student looking down because he does not know the answer
findings.explanation: The English invents Kuzuki as the possessor of a question, turning a simile into an interaction.

findings.highlight: I stand on one foot like a scarecrow.
findings.evidenceJa: 歩くことすらできず立ち尽くす
findings.governingReading: Unable even to walk, I remain standing frozen
findings.explanation: The mature-text branch inserts a one-legged scarecrow image absent from the active Japanese.
The surreal disbelief of the fatal impact becomes comic absurdity.
